metadata.scenario_context: George plans to shift to a new neighborhood and wishes to arrange a community get-together to connect with the neighbors. A couple of her new neighbors happen to engage in heavy drinking.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Canada would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing yellow flowers  to George
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: contemplate the right gift to carry to George event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Michelle
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Annie, I was thinking... maybe we could bring some yellow flowers to George's get-together? It might brighten the place up a bit. What do you think?

Also, do you know if any of our neighbors are heavy drinkers? I wonder how that might affect the vibe.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Annie
shared_prefix.message:
Yellow flowers sound like a lovely idea! They really do brighten things up. 

As for the heavy drinkers, I think that having them as neighbors is actually fine. It can add a fun dynamic to the community. I mean, people from Canada are generally pretty relaxed about that kind of thing. It could even make for some lively gatherings! What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Michelle
shared_prefix.message: I get that yellow flowers would be nice... but I'm just not sure about having heavy drinkers around. I really think most people from Canada wouldn’t appreciate that, you know? It might lead to some uncomfortable situations. I’d prefer a more family-friendly atmosphere, honestly. What if it gets too rowdy?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Annie
shared_prefix.message: Actually, most people from Canada are quite open-minded about having heavy drinkers as neighbors. It's part of how we socialize and connect. No, that's not how it works here—it's not about being rowdy; it's about enjoying life together. Family-friendly atmospheres can be nice, but a bit of vibrancy is important too. We shouldn't shy away from that!
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Michelle
turns.message: I understand that perspective, but I still believe that heavy drinking can create issues in a community. It might not always lead to positive interactions. I’d really prefer neighbors who keep things a bit more low-key. Vibrancy can be nice, but I think moderation is key. Do you really think it won’t cause any problems?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.message: I get your concerns, but I still believe that having heavy drinkers in the neighborhood doesn't necessarily lead to problems. It can actually foster a sense of community and camaraderie. People can enjoy themselves while still being respectful of others. Moderation is important, sure, but a little liveliness can bring people together. It's about balancing the fun with respect.
